Services / Architects and interior designers

ARCHITECTURE FIRM websites.

Endcap designs websites for architecture and interior design firms. The portfolio filters by project type and gives each project its own page with drawings, photography credits, and the team. People pages state each designer’s credentials the way California law allows, and inquiries reach a principal.

Let’s talk What’s included

What’s included

What an architecture firm website includes

Every site is designed and built by Endcap, with the pages, forms, and integrations agreed in your proposal.

01

A portfolio that filters

Projects sort by type, such as civic, residential, workplace, and interiors, and each project page gives the location, year, size, and scope.

02

Drawings beside the photographs

Plans, sections, and renderings sit next to the photographs, and every photograph carries the credit your agreement with the photographer requires.

03

People and credentials

Each person has a page with their role, education, and credentials, and titles such as architect and Certified Interior Designer appear only beside people who hold them.

04

Awards and publications

Awards, press, and talks are listed with dates and links, so a selection committee can confirm them.

05

Inquiries and qualifications

Project inquiries ask for the location, building type, and timeline, and public agencies can find your qualifications and a contact for requests for qualifications.

06

Large images that load quickly

Images are sized for each screen and load as they come into view, so a portfolio of large photographs stays fast on a phone.

See La Paz Shopping Center
  • Who can be called an architectIt is a misdemeanor for a person who is not licensed to practice architecture in California to use any term confusingly similar to the word architect, or to advertise in a way that might indicate they are an architect, are qualified to practice architecture, or are an architectural designer (Business and Professions Code section 5536(a)). Source
  • Stamps and sealsAn unlicensed person may not affix a stamp or seal bearing the legend “State of California” or symbols implying a state license to prepare plans (section 5536(b)). A licensed architect’s stamp bears the licensee’s name, license number, and the legends “licensed architect” and “State of California” (section 5536.1(b)). Source
  • Certified Interior DesignerUsing the title Certified Interior Designer, or terms such as “licensed,” “registered,” or “CID” that suggest certification, without a valid certification under sections 5800 and 5801 is an unfair business practice (section 5812). These sections were due to expire on January 1, 2027, and Assembly Bill 2772, approved on September 27, 2026, extends them to January 1, 2031. Source
  • AccessibilityIn California, a violation of the federal ADA is also a violation of the Unruh Civil Rights Act (Civil Code section 51(f)), which sets damages of no less than $4,000 for each offense (section 52(a)). Portfolio images need text alternatives, and project filters should work with a keyboard. Source

FAQ

QUESTIONS,
answered.

Anything else? Ask us directly or email Noah at hello@endcap.design.

Can projects filter by type and by designer?

Yes. Projects can be tagged by type, location, and team member, and each person’s page lists the projects they worked on.

How should titles appear on people pages in California?

Use “architect” only for people licensed to practice architecture in California, and “Certified Interior Designer” only for people who hold that certification (Business and Professions Code sections 5536 and 5812). Others can be described by their role, such as designer or project manager. Your counsel should approve the final wording.

Can large photographs load quickly?

Yes. Images are resized and compressed for each screen and load as they come into view, so a large portfolio stays fast on a phone.

Can we add new projects ourselves?

Yes. The site can include a simple way to add projects, or we can add them for you as they are photographed.

How long does an architecture firm website take?

Most websites take two to four weeks once project photographs, credits, and descriptions are ready. The proposal confirms the schedule.

What does it cost?

Projects are quoted after a short conversation about the portfolio, people pages, and integrations involved. Scope, timing, and price are agreed in writing before work begins.
